The feedback loop acts on a
replica of the input stage.
The input stage is copied,
with the same transistor
sizes and currents. The
corresponding inputs are
connected. The outputs of
the replicas are shorted to
cancel out the differential
signals. In this way, the total
current is measured in such
a pair, regardless of whether
it is on, off or halfway.
The averaged outputs
now lead to current mirrors
to be summed towards
point S.
Replica is an ideal way to bias transistors without actually contacting the sensitive nodes, and
without feedback. A few more examples are given.
commentary_segments.text: The feedback loop acts on a replica of the input stage. The input stage is copied, with the same transistor sizes and currents. The corresponding inputs are connected. The outputs of the replicas are shorted to cancel out the differential signals. In this way, the total current is measured in such a pair, regardless of whether it is on, off or halfway. The averaged outputs now lead to current mirrors to be summed towards point S. Replica is an ideal way to bias transistors without actually contacting the sensitive nodes, and without feedback. A few more examples are given.
